draft_evidence.quote: He had felt empty. He had felt the hollow a spent framework left, ten times over, on a rim two days ago; that was empty, and this was not that.

comparison_evidence.quote: ## After Chapter 19 (CLOSED — PASS r2; 5,289 words; spliced 2026-09-04) — the Long Stair, the trap (the 114th)

findings.consequence: The only rim in the sequence is the Long Stair's, where the Daeva suite was spent and STATE_RUNNING records Cael 'all ten hollow' — the trap on the 114th, the chamber day on the 115th. Chapter 21 then puts the Drowned Hall three days further along the bearing, and this passage is written on the night the draft itself dates as the hundred and nineteenth (line 43). The rim is therefore four to five days behind, not two. A reader who has been given a dated log on the page in every chapter of this book is being asked to hold two incompatible intervals in the same paragraph, and the repair run's whole subject was making this chapter's calendar hold.
findings.repair_target: Correct the interval to the number the draft's own dateline and the state ledger produce (four to five days, or an unnumbered reference to the rim) without moving the 119th/120th dating that the third-reading repair now depends on.

draft_evidence.quote: It had been there before Oryn; session nine was five years old and she was ten weeks.

comparison_evidence.quote: - Timeline: the ledge collapses at first light on the SEVENTY-EIGHTH day past the Line; the party waits in the fin's lee through the seventy-eighth and seventy-ninth; Oryn arrives on the morning of the EIGHTIETH day (the second day after the collapse); the log's one line is dated the eightieth day.

findings.consequence: Oryn walked up the road on the eightieth day past the Line; the entry is written on the hundred and nineteenth. That is thirty-nine days — five and a half weeks — not ten. The sentence is the chapter's central act of counting, set deliberately against 'five years old', and it is the counting protagonist's own arithmetic; a reader tracking the day-numbered log entries the book has printed since Chapter 1 will find the one number in the sentence that can be checked is nearly double.
findings.repair_target: Replace 'ten weeks' with the interval the state ledger produces from the eightieth day to the hundred and nineteenth, or with an unnumbered comparison that keeps the five-years-against-weeks contrast intact.

draft_evidence.quote: he had learned it from a woman thirty strides back along the track with a straightedge she had not laid along anything for two days. *I cannot find the banks.* Not *there are no banks.* The reading was hers and it was ten days his,

comparison_evidence.quote: He had the reading. He had had it awake at contact range for three weeks and had put it on one person who had asked him to and on himself,

findings.consequence: Two counts in one line fail against the chapter's own dating. The straightedge was last laid along the carter's map at the Stair's rim (ch21.md line 5, and repaired into this draft at line 131), which the state ledger dates to the hundred and fifteenth; on the hundred and nineteenth that is four days idle, not two — and this clause is one of the eight spans the repair rewrote, so the corrected sentence has carried in a new wrong interval. Separately, the tenth fragment is given two different ages inside one chapter: 'ten days his' here against 'for three weeks' at line 99, the latter of which is the one that matches the hundredth-day acquisition. A reader who noticed the instrument's age in the Teague scene will find it contradicted in the self-reading forty lines earlier.
findings.repair_target: Bring both intervals onto the draft's own calendar: the straightedge idle since the Stair's rim on the hundred and fifteenth, and the reading's age stated once, consistently with the 'three weeks' at line 99 and the hundredth-day acquisition.

concerns: Injury specificity lost in the repair, not a defect: r1 carried Cael's Hall bill twice, once in the opening order and once in Oryn's deleted speech ('Ribs are ribs. They've had a bill and they're paying it'). The speech had to go with the reading's reversal, and the ribs now appear exactly once, at line 3, as one of three things Oryn said two days to. Persistence holds, but the wound has stopped costing anything the reader can feel. A four-word restoration somewhere in the Teague movement would put it back without touching the repaired scenes.

Judgment call for a human, not filed as a finding: Oryn's stated reason for the inversion — 'I want to hear it said with your hand on me, so that I can feel whether the thing telling it is steady' (line 55), paid off at line 63 as her feeling him through his own hand — is a Tide capability the taught readings do not quite cover. Ch7 defines both depths as the healer's hands on the patient and her current run through him; here she is the one being touched and reads through it. It is consistent with the contact-range rule and it resolves nothing, so the packet's approval_required clause on 'any Tide mechanic beyond the taught readings' may or may not bite. It is worth an owner's yes or no before Ch23 leans on it.

No bill is shown for Cael's own use of the reading. Three uses in this chapter — two hours alone and a minute on Oryn's wrist — and the only after-state is 'when his hands had stopped being a healer's and had gone back to being his' (line 41). Section 6.2's cost vocabulary includes attention budget, and Ch21 priced the Iron read in exactly that currency; an hour of the tenth fragment costing nothing at all is the one place in the chapter where the series' bill-for-everything discipline is quieter than usual. The constraints are all present, so this is calibration rather than a violated contract.

Ear check, watch rather than fix: Ternhall and Thornwater co-occur in this chapter for the first time (lines 131 and 3/47). The registry rates neither as a collision and the vowels and second elements differ, but they share the T-r-n skeleton and Ternhall has not been said aloud since Book 3. If a narrator stumbles, Ternhall is the cheaper side.

Forward risk outside this chapter's scope: Karis's brass folding straightedge is now firmly established as hers, carried out of Ternhall and used at the Stair's rim (line 131). The Chapter 24 card gives Hesk's late birthday package as 'instrument-maker's work, a straightedge, brass, folding'. Two brass folding straightedges on one inn table will read as a duplication rather than a gift; the collision should be resolved at the architecture layer before Ch24 drafts.

Taste only, carried from r1 and unchanged: the river-and-stone image and the instrument-limit distinction are stated in the narration, restated in the telling to Oryn, and restated again in the log. The repetition is motivated by the no-deflection brief and by Cael's method, and the third statement is the shortest, but the middle of the movement still reads more confirmatory than exploratory.
strengths: The repair improves the scene it was asked only to correct. Inverting the reading turns a passive examination into a transaction with three moving parts — she sets the terms, he asks, she answers, and she gets her own reading of him through the contact anyway. 'Not me in you. You in me' is a better first line for the movement than the one it replaced, and 'at my count and not yours' keeps the rationing of a healer's reserve visible without spending any.

Consent is rendered as procedure rather than sentiment, and the procedure is recorded. The wrist held out and not put in his hand, the question asked before the touch, and the log entry made 'smaller, that he had asked and she had said yes, in that order, which was the order' (line 69) make the ask-first rule an act with paperwork. This is the same discipline the series uses for the Power Log and it is exactly the right place for it.

The Teague fire scene survives the repair untouched and remains the chapter's strongest movement. The one-foot wrist distance, the itemised ledger of what each depth would return, the hand that stays on the track, and the human question offered in place of the instrument make the moral stake behavioural. The fixed log line then records conduct instead of congratulating it.

The reveal boundary is protected with unusual explicitness. '*I cannot find the banks.* Not *there are no banks.*' separates the instrument's limit from a fact about the architecture in nine words, and the still place stays shape, location and behaviour — never source, never age, never name — with the refusal to guess stated as method rather than as restraint.

Yes, the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. Nothing is explained: the two reading depths appear as hand placement, a count of ten, a rationed minute, and the requirement that a subject be still and willing; the board and the registry appear as two prices for the same man's work; research appears as eleven, twenty-nine and twelve sheets, a ledger open at an unfinished line, a straightedge moved a hair, and the sound of a pencil.

There is no fight, as the packet requires, and the set piece is nevertheless choreographed and memorable: a fire, two men side by side, and a wrist twelve inches from a hand that could answer the question being asked. Its win sentence is writable — Cael removed the reading's ability to turn Teague into an answer by keeping his hand on the track and asking instead — which is more than most fights in this book manage in a paragraph.

The injury and possession seam is handled with economy. Brom's shoulder is at 'Twice', which is the exact number Oryn's Ch21 order allows, and the visiting healer's 'Then it wants binding, not hands' converts that order into an action performed by a stranger who has never heard it. Lira keeps the bolt in the bow. Oryn sleeps four hours in front of people for the first time.

The close earns its place as an image. Distance, a second fire, a number and a number and a number, the scratch of an edge being set — and then the absence of the sound. Chapter 23's finding gets its pressure without a word of explanation, and the beat type differs cleanly from Chapter 21's dialogue close.

Production is clean and the repair did not disturb it. 4,015 words inside the 3,910-5,290 band; every Section 9 capped phrase at zero; no pitch-family use added to the book's exhausted cap; metadata, summary-substitution, modern-register, feeling-declaration and growth-declaration greps all zero; one single-word paragraph against a cap of two; attribution survives audio in the one three-party exchange; and the diff against r1 is confined to the three repair targets.
